transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes (recording started a few seconds late)
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan, Sana, Tom, Maya (Lighthouse Retail)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on reconstructing request paths, using hop-maps for request forensics, replaying requests via the trace export, and designing a fallback orchestration strategy for inference fallbacks (model variant routing, regional failover). Security questions covered KMS, audit logs, and SAML SSO. Action items and a staging benchmark were agreed.

Topics: request-path autopsy; hop-mapping; trace export + replay; KV/prefix cache eviction; fallback orchestration; security (KMS/audit/SOC2); pricing/poC next steps

--- Transcript (selected excerpts, timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Jared: hey everyone uh thanks for joining, this is Jared from Redwood—i'll hand it to Priya for the deep walk — she runs a lot of the debugging playbooks so you'll see the console in action.
[00:12] Priya: hi all, thanks. quick agenda: we'll show how to stitch a request path across services, identify where tokens/kv cache misses happen, run a trace export, and then demo a replay into staging so you can validate fallback behavior.
[00:25] Evan: cool — our main ask is to reduce P99 latency spikes and understand cases where users get partial answers or 502s. also we have to prove no customer text leaves our VPC in the pilot.
[00:34] Priya: noted — privacy/residency is a config we'll demo via private deployment settings.
[00:39] Sana: quick security note — our compliance team will want to see KMS integration and an immutable audit trail for each request.
[00:44] Jared: absolutely, Tom and I have the SOC2 pack, but Priya will show live logs too.
[00:49] [01:05] Priya: okay sharing screen — this is the Console, top-left is Request Explorer. i'll search by the correlation id you gave earlier, evan?
[01:12] Evan: yeah it's r-20271109-8341.
[01:18] Priya: searching... there's a cluster of requests around 11:12 UTC — looks like a spike. i'll open the hop-map.
[01:27] Priya: hop-map shows the request flow: edge proxy -> auth-service -> inference-router -> dedicated-gpu-pool -> fallback-proxy -> db-write. you can hover to see timings and the per-hop token counts.
[01:40] Sana: that 'fallback-proxy' node — is that Redwood's routing fallback or our app-level handler?
[01:45] Priya: good question, it's Redwood's fallback orchestrator in this setup — we route to a cheaper quantized variant if the primary model is overloaded, then fall back to a regional model if latency SLO is breached. the orchestration policy is visible in the route config.
[01:59] Tom: are KV cache misses visible? we suspect cache thrash is causing retries and extra token charges.
[02:05] Priya: yes — in the hop detail you can see cache hit/miss ratio and the KV key namespace. see here — eviction events pop with their timestamps.
[02:15] Priya: notice a 503 from inference-router at 11:12:22 then a retry which traveled to the fallback-proxy. you can expand the request inspector to see the raw payload and the partial generated tokens.
[02:30] Evan: i'm seeing some weird model names — the transcriber wrote 'redwood-compact-3b' but our manifests say 'redwood-compact-v3'; is that a transcription thing?
[02:36] Priya: mmh, sometimes the naming in the manifest and the runtime variant differ; we'll reconcile that in the trace export. it's common to have aliasing which makes ops hunts tricky.
[02:45] [05:00] Priya: i'll now run an export of the full trace bundle — this includes request headers, server-side logs, and the per-token latency table. the export link is time-limited and encrypted by your KMS key if you have it configured.
[05:14] Tom: perfect — show the KMS step.
[05:17] Priya: here under Security > Integrations, you can map a customer KMS ARN. when enabled, export artifacts are encrypted and the console shows which key was used. audit events are logged for each export.
[05:30] Maya: what about SSO? we use Okta.
[05:33] Jared: SAML/Okta is supported — we can send an SSO metadata file and the admin roles map to RBAC in the Console.
[05:43] [08:10] Priya: switching to replay mode — you can replay a request into a staging cluster. we'll do a dry-run first: replay with header x-redwood-test: true to avoid downstream side effects. this replays the original token stream but with deterministic inputs so you can test fallbacks.
[08:28] Priya: starting dry-run... watch the request table — notice the hop timings shrink because staging is smaller, but the fallback orchestration path triggers the quantized model correctly at 11:12:22 equivalent.
[08:45] Sana: is the replay exact? like will it re-use the same KV cache contents?
[08:50] Priya: by default replay replays the request only — KV state is not mutated unless you opt into stateful replay. we have a 'preserve-kv' flag but for safety most teams run replay isolated.
[09:05] Evan: this policing of state is great — for our main pilot we won't allow live writes.
[09:12] [12:00] Priya: quick aside on sampling — the Console can sample traces using a custom rule set: e.g., sample on errors, or sample N% of traffic for higher-level baselines. that reduces storage and costs while keeping high-fidelity on failures.
[12:20] Tom: if we sample some errors, will we miss cascades that start as warnings?
[12:25] Priya: you can set multi-trigger sampling — error OR spike-in-latency triggers a full trace capture. we usually recommend 1% baseline + 100% on error for production.
[12:38] [15:30] Priya: now the debug: i'm going to correlate request logs with our observability export — notice a series of auth timeouts prior to the 503, auth-service returned 401 then retried leading to extra token consumption.
[15:47] Evan: ah — that matches a config mismatch our auth team rolled out last week. so the extra retries propagated down to inference and caused the fallback.
[16:00] Priya: exactly — the Console shows parent->child relationship; you can collapse sub-requests to see the root cause. this helps when many microservices are involved.
[16:15] Maya: can we plug into our existing datadog traces?
[16:18] Priya: yes — we ingest trace IDs and can stitch to external APM via the trace ID. we also export OpenTelemetry spans. sometimes the span names differ slightly which causes fuzzy matching, but it works in most flows.
[16:30] [19:45] Priya: we'll demo a 'what-if' fallback policy change — currently policy says: primary -> quantized-variant -> regional-fallback. i'll flip to direct regional-first for a short window to show policy rollouts.
[19:58] Priya: apply rollout — policy applied to 10% of traffic by tag 'pilot-lhr'. watch the hop map.
[20:10] Evan: neat — that avoids the quantized step for tagged sessions, but what about token cost implications?
[20:16] Priya: you'll see token count and cost estimate on the route page; the Console projects cost delta based on historic token distributions. that helps you decide tradeoffs.
[20:32] Tom: procurement will want per-route pricing.
[20:36] Jared: we'll include per-route cost projections in the quote.
[20:40] [24:00] Priya: showing timeline view now — there's a neat 'request playback' ribbon that shows error annotations, deployment version at the time, and any model-variant switchovers. if you click an annotation it opens the exact payload.
[24:15] Sana: are retention windows configurable? legal will ask for 90 days minimum.
[24:20] Priya: yes — Console retention can be set per-tenant; long-retention is an add-on. exports before deletion are possible and are encrypted.
[24:32] [28:10] Priya: demoing filters — we can filter by response code, model-variant, region, and also by 'cache-miss-rate>10%'. that was clincher for other retail customers.
[28:25] Evan: about private deployment — we need to keep traffic inside our VPC and control keys. is full on-prem supported?
[28:33] Jared: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package. KMS/HSM integrations are supported; key material never leaves your control plane if you choose customer-managed keys.
[28:50] Maya: we have strict egress rules; can we pin to a single region for the pilot?
[28:54] Priya: absolutely — routing policies can pin traffic by org tag and enforce regional residency.
[29:05] [32:20] Priya: performance note — KV cache cold-starts matter: if your workload has diverse prompts, cold starts spike until the cache warms. we typically recommend a warm-up phase in the PoC with synthetic traces to prime KV.
[32:35] Evan: ok we'd need a warm-up script.
[32:39] Priya: we'll share a sample script in the follow-up.
[32:50] [36:00] Priya: now i want to show a failure forensics flow: take a request that produced a truncated response — Console shows partial tokens and the token cutoff reason (e.g., "max_tokens reached" vs "timeout"). here the reason is timeout at the GPU level.
[36:20] Sana: do you surface GPU metrics?
[36:23] Priya: yes — per-host GPU utilization, queue length, and average token latencies. we align those with the request timeline. you can also tag hosts to isolate a noisy neighbor.
[36:35] Tom: our compliance wants proof that raw prompts are never logged in plaintext to long-retention storage.
[36:40] Priya: by default the Console redacts PII and can hash or redact prompt contents; full raw payload retention is opt-in with explicit KMS and legal approvals.
[36:55] [40:10] Priya: a couple of caveats — transcription in the Console can mislabel runtime variants if you have multiple alias levels. we suggest consistent manifest naming and a nightly job to sync aliases to improve trace clarity.
[40:30] Evan: that explains the mismatch earlier. we'll add an alias-sync job.
[40:36] [44:00] Priya: wrapping up with runbook automation: you can attach a runbook to a route so that when a particular error cluster occurs, the Console suggests runbook steps and can even open a PagerDuty incident with pre-populated diagnostics.
[44:20] Maya: can runbooks be authored by our ops team?
[44:23] Priya: yes — they are markdown files with variable interpolation, and you can scope them to route tags.
[44:30] [48:00] Jared: ok final security recap — we'll send SOC2 report and network diagram. tom, you'll get KMS docs and the export encryption details.
[48:12] Tom: thanks — also want an architecture note on audit log immutability.
[48:18] Jared: we'll include the audit log retention and immutability section in the pack.
[48:25] [52:15] Priya: last demo snippet — error clustering: Console groups similar failures by fingerprint (stack-ish), you can bulk-ack and attach a fix. this was helpful for a retail customer who had 200 duplicate incidents and reduced noise by 80%.
[52:35] Evan: that's good for our ops team.
[52:40] Maya: timeline — we'd like a PoC for 4 weeks starting Dec 6, pending procurement approval.
[52:50] Jared: sounds reasonable — we'll aim to get the quote and staging access details in the next 48 hours.
[53:02] [58:00] Priya: i'll drop sample commands: how to export traces, a curl for the replay dry-run, and the warm-up script. expect links in the follow-up email.
[58:18] Evan: any blockers from a security perspective?
[58:22] Tom: not yet — we need the KMS integration doc and assurance on audit immutability.
[58:30] Jared: you will have that.
[58:35] [61:00] Jared: thanks everyone, that wraps it. we'll follow up with the artifacts and the quote.

Recap / Notes:
- Root cause for the spike: auth timeouts increased retries -> kv-cache churn -> inference-router 503 -> fallback triggered.
- Recommended PoC steps: enable staging, run KV warm-up, replay blocked requests in dry-run, validate fallback policy by toggling rollout.
- Security: customer-managed KMS for exports, SAML SSO with RBAC, audit logs immutable (add-on).

Attached/Referenced artifacts (links to be sent post-call):
- trace-export-sample.tar.gpg (KMS encrypted)
- PoC warm-up script (shell + synthetic payloads)
- SOC2 + KMS integration guide (PDF)
- Pilot pricing + per-route cost projection (spreadsheet)

End of transcript.
